title: Does the image modality break the refusal link in vision-language models?

original_idea.body: On a small open VLM, extract a text-based refusal direction and measure the modality gap in refusal effectiveness for image-borne vs text-borne harm; single consumer GPU.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: text-built refusal directions failing on image-borne harm targets a fast-growing multimodal attack surface (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: VLM setup and cross-modal direction application adds complexity beyond a text probe (level 3).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable (modality gap) but VLM curation adds dependency (level 4).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Image-borne jailbreaks are lab-underserved; neglected multimodal safety work (level 5).

low_compute.reasoning: Small open VLM inference on a single consumer GPU; mid-range.

novelty.reasoning: Text-to-image refusal-direction modality gap appears mostly novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Text-to-image refusal modality gap appears mostly novel.
